pois.line: A flat tin under a slate slab, left by someone who knew these hills well and trusted nobody else to.

lore: The wind drops when you stand beside it. You do not mention this to anyone.
The real thing is Callanish, on the Isle of Lewis: a cross of standing stones about 5,000 years old.

pois.line: This is a private camp. Private as in 'mind your own'.
A hollow behind a rock, and a lunchbox in the hollow. Whoever left it knew what they were doing, and was not coming back for it.
You didn't see us. We didn't see you. Except now we have.

lore: It is cold, and it hums very faintly, the way a fridge does.
The real thing is Machrie Moor, on the Isle of Arran: a moor full of rings, one with a tall granite slab.

pois.line: A flask-sized tin under a flat stone, tied with garden twine. Someone's emergency tea. You are an emergency.

lore: Sheep have rubbed one side smooth. Even the sheep come here.
The real thing is the Ring of Brodgar, on Orkney: a huge ring of upright slabs on a spit between two lochs.
You put a hand on it. It is older than your whole family tree, put together.
The real thing is the Clava Cairns, near Inverness: ring cairns inside circles of standing stones, among old beech trees.

pois.line: A hollow in the old tree, and something wrapped in oilcloth.
Behind the rock there is a gap, and in the gap there is a lunchbox. Inside, a bonnet, folded very neatly.

lore: Lichen has been at it for a few thousand years and has barely got started.
The real thing is Callanish, on the Isle of Lewis: a cross of standing stones about 5,000 years old.

pois.line: This is a private camp. Private as in 'mind your own'.
A biscuit tin, wedged behind the rock. The lid took three goes.

lore: The wind drops when you stand beside it. You do not mention this to anyone.
The real thing is the Ring of Brodgar, on Orkney: a huge ring of upright slabs on a spit between two lochs.
